```{r}
# SPlit Data for training and testing set

library(rsample)

# Set seed for reproducibility
set.seed(123)

# Split data, keeping outcome proportions similar
heart_split <- initial_split(
  heart_clean,
  prop = 0.80,
  strata = heart_disease
)

# Create training and testing datasets
heart_train <- training(heart_split)
heart_test <- testing(heart_split)

# Check dimensions
dim(heart_train)
dim(heart_test)

# Check outcome distribution
table(heart_train$heart_disease)
table(heart_test$heart_disease)
```

```{r}
# Handling Missing Values Using K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) Imputation
# KNN estimates missing values using information from similar patients.

# Load required packages
library(recipes)
library(dplyr)

# Convert categorical variables to factors
categorical <- c(
  "sex", "cp", "fbs", "restecg",
  "exang", "slope", "ca", "thal",
  "hospital"
)

for (col in categorical) {

  heart_train[[col]] <- factor(heart_train[[col]])

  heart_test[[col]] <- factor(
    heart_test[[col]],
    levels = levels(heart_train[[col]])
  )
}

# Create preprocessing recipe using KNN imputation
# neighbors = 5 means the five most similar patients are used

heart_recipe <- recipe(
  heart_disease ~ .,
  data = heart_train
) %>%
  step_impute_knn(
    all_predictors(),
    neighbors = 5
  )

# Learn preprocessing information from training data only
heart_prep <- prep(
  heart_recipe,
  training = heart_train
)

# Apply KNN imputation to training data
train_ready <- bake(
  heart_prep,
  new_data = heart_train
)

# Apply the same preprocessing to testing data
test_ready <- bake(
  heart_prep,
  new_data = heart_test
)

# Check remaining missing values in training data
cat("Missing values in training data:\n")
print(colSums(is.na(train_ready)))

# Check remaining missing values in testing data
cat("\nMissing values in testing data:\n")
print(colSums(is.na(test_ready)))

# Check total missing values
cat("\nTotal missing values in training data:",
    sum(is.na(train_ready)), "\n")

cat("Total missing values in testing data:",
    sum(is.na(test_ready)), "\n")

# Display dimensions of processed datasets
cat("\nTraining data dimensions:",
    dim(train_ready), "\n")

cat("Testing data dimensions:",
    dim(test_ready), "\n")
```


```{r}
# Logistic Regression Model Using KNN-Imputed Data

# Remove hospital variable, as in the previous model
train_final <- train_ready[, !names(train_ready) %in% "hospital"]
test_final  <- test_ready[, !names(test_ready) %in% "hospital"]

# Train Logistic Regression model
logistic_model <- glm(
  heart_disease ~ .,
  data = train_final,
  family = binomial
)

# Predict probability of heart disease
logistic_prob <- predict(
  logistic_model,
  newdata = test_final,
  type = "response"
)

# Correct predicted class labels
logistic_pred <- factor(
  ifelse(logistic_prob >= 0.5, "No_Disease", "Disease"),
  levels = levels(test_final$heart_disease)
)

# Confusion matrix
logistic_cm <- table(
  Actual = test_final$heart_disease,
  Predicted = logistic_pred
)

print(logistic_cm)

# Calculate accuracy
logistic_accuracy <- mean(
  logistic_pred == test_final$heart_disease
)

cat(
  "\nLogistic Regression Accuracy:",
  round(logistic_accuracy * 100, 2),
  "%\n"
)
```


```{r}
# Random Forest Classification Using KNN-Imputed Data

library(randomForest)

# Set seed for reproducibility
set.seed(123)

# Train Random Forest model
rf_model <- randomForest(
  heart_disease ~ .,
  data = train_final,
  ntree = 500,
  importance = TRUE
)

# Predict heart disease classes
rf_pred <- predict(
  rf_model,
  newdata = test_final,
  type = "response"
)

# Confusion matrix
rf_cm <- table(
  Actual = test_final$heart_disease,
  Predicted = rf_pred
)

print(rf_cm)

# Calculate accuracy
rf_accuracy <- mean(
  rf_pred == test_final$heart_disease
)

cat(
  "\nRandom Forest Accuracy:",
  round(rf_accuracy * 100, 2),
  "%\n"
)
```

```{r}
# Calculating the evaluation Metrics

# Compare Logistic Regression and Random Forest Performance

calculate_metrics <- function(actual, predicted) {

  actual <- as.character(actual)
  predicted <- as.character(predicted)

  TP <- sum(actual == "Disease" & predicted == "Disease")
  TN <- sum(actual == "No_Disease" & predicted == "No_Disease")
  FP <- sum(actual == "No_Disease" & predicted == "Disease")
  FN <- sum(actual == "Disease" & predicted == "No_Disease")

  accuracy <- (TP + TN) / (TP + TN + FP + FN)
  sensitivity <- TP / (TP + FN)
  specificity <- TN / (TN + FP)
  precision <- TP / (TP + FP)
  f1_score <- 2 * precision * sensitivity / (precision + sensitivity)

  return(c(
    Accuracy = accuracy,
    Sensitivity = sensitivity,
    Specificity = specificity,
    Precision = precision,
    F1_Score = f1_score
  ))
}

# Logistic Regression metrics
logistic_metrics <- calculate_metrics(
  test_final$heart_disease,
  logistic_pred
)

# Random Forest metrics
rf_metrics <- calculate_metrics(
  test_final$heart_disease,
  rf_pred
)

# Create comparison table
model_comparison <- data.frame(
  Metric = names(logistic_metrics),
  Logistic_Regression = round(logistic_metrics * 100, 2),
  Random_Forest = round(rf_metrics * 100, 2)
)

print(model_comparison)
```
```{r}
# Visual Comparison of Classification Models

library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)

# Convert comparison table to long format
comparison_long <- model_comparison %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(Logistic_Regression, Random_Forest),
    names_to = "Model",
    values_to = "Score"
  )

# Improve model labels

  comparison_long$Model,
  levels = c("Logistic_Regression", "Random_Forest"),
  labels = c("Logistic Regression", "Random Forest")
)

# Create grouped bar chart
ggplot(
  comparison_long,
  aes(x = Metric, y = Score, fill = Model)
) +
  geom_col(
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),
    width = 0.7
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = paste0(Score, "%")),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),
    vjust = -0.4,
    size = 3.5
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Logistic Regression" = "#4472C4",
      "Random Forest" = "#ED7D31"
    )
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 100),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Logistic Regression vs Random Forest",
    subtitle = "Heart Disease Classification Using KNN Imputation",
    x = "Evaluation Metric",
    y = "Performance (%)",
    fill = "Classification Model"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 25, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )
```

```{r}
# Logistic Regression Variable Importance
# Based on the increase in model deviance when each predictor is removed

library(ggplot2)

# Calculate importance for each predictor
logistic_importance <- drop1(
  logistic_model,
  test = "Chisq"
)

# Convert results to a data frame
logistic_importance_df <- data.frame(
  Variable = rownames(logistic_importance),
  Importance = logistic_importance$LRT
)

# Remove the overall model row
logistic_importance_df <- logistic_importance_df[
  logistic_importance_df$Variable != "<none>",
]

# Remove any missing values
logistic_importance_df <- na.omit(logistic_importance_df)

# Sort predictors by importance
logistic_importance_df <- logistic_importance_df[
  order(logistic_importance_df$Importance, decreasing = TRUE),
]
```

```{r}
# ROC Curve and AUC Comparison

library(pROC)
library(ggplot2)

# Logistic Regression predicted probabilities
logistic_prob <- predict(
  logistic_model,
  newdata = test_final,
  type = "response"
)

# Ensure probabilities represent heart disease
if (levels(logistic_model$model$heart_disease)[2] == "No_Disease") {
  logistic_prob <- 1 - logistic_prob
}

# Random Forest predicted probabilities
rf_prob <- predict(
  rf_model,
  newdata = test_final,
  type = "prob"
)[, "Disease"]

# Calculate Logistic Regression ROC
logistic_roc <- roc(
  response = test_final$heart_disease,
  predictor = logistic_prob,
  levels = c("No_Disease", "Disease"),
  direction = "<"
)

# Calculate Random Forest ROC
rf_roc <- roc(
  response = test_final$heart_disease,
  predictor = rf_prob,
  levels = c("No_Disease", "Disease"),
  direction = "<"
)

# Calculate AUC values
logistic_auc <- auc(logistic_roc)
rf_auc <- auc(rf_roc)

# Create AUC comparison table
auc_comparison <- data.frame(
  Model = c("Logistic Regression", "Random Forest"),
  AUC = round(
    c(as.numeric(logistic_auc), as.numeric(rf_auc)),
    4
  )
)

print(auc_comparison)
```

```{r}
# Five- fold Validation
set.seed(123)

# Prepare the original training dataset
cv_data <- heart_train

# Convert outcome to factor
cv_data$heart_disease <- factor(
  cv_data$heart_disease,
  levels = c("No_Disease", "Disease")
)

# Create stratified 5-fold cross-validation
cv_folds <- vfold_cv(
  cv_data,
  v = 5,
  strata = heart_disease
)

cv_folds
```
```{r}

#Train and evaluate both models across the five folds
## Function to calculate performance metrics

cv_metrics <- function(actual, probability) {

  predicted <- ifelse(
    probability >= 0.5,
    "Disease",
    "No_Disease"
  )

  TP <- sum(actual == "Disease" & predicted == "Disease")
  TN <- sum(actual == "No_Disease" & predicted == "No_Disease")
  FP <- sum(actual == "No_Disease" & predicted == "Disease")
  FN <- sum(actual == "Disease" & predicted == "No_Disease")

  accuracy <- (TP + TN) / (TP + TN + FP + FN)
  sensitivity <- TP / (TP + FN)
  specificity <- TN / (TN + FP)
  precision <- TP / (TP + FP)

  f1 <- 2 * TP / (2 * TP + FP + FN)

  auc_value <- as.numeric(
    pROC::auc(
      pROC::roc(
        actual,
        probability,
        levels = c("No_Disease", "Disease"),
        direction = "<",
        quiet = TRUE
      )
    )
  )

  data.frame(
    Accuracy = accuracy,
    Sensitivity = sensitivity,
    Specificity = specificity,
    Precision = precision,
    F1_Score = f1,
    AUC = auc_value
  )
}
```


```{r}

#Perform the cross-validation
set.seed(123)

cv_results <- data.frame()

for (i in seq_len(nrow(cv_folds))) {

  # Extract training and validation subsets
  fold_train <- analysis(cv_folds$splits[[i]])
  fold_valid <- assessment(cv_folds$splits[[i]])

  # Create KNN imputation recipe
  fold_recipe <- recipe(
    heart_disease ~ .,
    data = fold_train
  ) %>%
    step_impute_knn(
      all_predictors(),
      neighbors = 5
    )

  # Fit imputation using only fold training data
  fold_prep <- prep(
    fold_recipe,
    training = fold_train
  )

  # Apply imputation
  fold_train_ready <- bake(
    fold_prep,
    new_data = fold_train
  )

  fold_valid_ready <- bake(
    fold_prep,
    new_data = fold_valid
  )

  # Remove hospital before model training
  fold_train_final <- fold_train_ready %>%
    select(-hospital)

  fold_valid_final <- fold_valid_ready %>%
    select(-hospital)

  # Train Logistic Regression
  fold_logistic <- glm(
    heart_disease ~ .,
    data = fold_train_final,
    family = binomial
  )

  # Train Random Forest
  fold_rf <- randomForest(
    heart_disease ~ .,
    data = fold_train_final,
    ntree = 500,
    importance = TRUE
  )

  # Logistic Regression probabilities
  fold_logistic_prob <- predict(
    fold_logistic,
    newdata = fold_valid_final,
    type = "response"
  )

  # Random Forest probabilities
  fold_rf_prob <- predict(
    fold_rf,
    newdata = fold_valid_final,
    type = "prob"
  )[, "Disease"]

  # Evaluate Logistic Regression
  lr_results <- cv_metrics(
    fold_valid_final$heart_disease,
    fold_logistic_prob
  )

  lr_results$Model <- "Logistic Regression"
  lr_results$Fold <- i

  # Evaluate Random Forest
  rf_results <- cv_metrics(
    fold_valid_final$heart_disease,
    fold_rf_prob
  )

  rf_results$Model <- "Random Forest"
  rf_results$Fold <- i

  # Store results
  cv_results <- bind_rows(
    cv_results,
    lr_results,
    rf_results
  )

  cat("Fold", i, "completed\n")
}

print(cv_results)
```


```{r}
#AUC Confidence Intervals and Statistical Comparison
# Calculate 95% AUC confidence intervals

logistic_ci <- pROC::ci.auc(
  logistic_roc,
  conf.level = 0.95,
  method = "delong"
)

rf_ci <- pROC::ci.auc(
  rf_roc,
  conf.level = 0.95,
  method = "delong"
)

# Create confidence interval comparison table

auc_ci_table <- data.frame(
  Model = c("Logistic Regression", "Random Forest"),
  AUC = c(
    as.numeric(logistic_auc),
    as.numeric(rf_auc)
  ),
  Lower_95_CI = c(logistic_ci[1], rf_ci[1]),
  Upper_95_CI = c(logistic_ci[3], rf_ci[3])
)

knitr::kable(
  auc_ci_table,
  digits = 4,
  caption = "ROC-AUC estimates with 95% confidence intervals"
)
```


```{r}
#Visualize the confidence intervals
ggplot(
  auc_ci_table,
  aes(x = Model, y = AUC, color = Model)
) +

      ymax = Upper_95_CI

    subtitle = "Held-out test dataset (n = 185)",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Area Under the ROC Curve"
  ) +

  theme(

  )
```

```{r}

#Perform DeLong's test We want to determine whether there is sufficient statistical evidence of a difference.

#- Null hypothesis (H₀): There is no difference between the AUC values of the two models.
#- Alternative hypothesis (H₁): There is a difference between the AUC values of the two models.
# Paired DeLong's test

delong_test <- pROC::roc.test(
  logistic_roc,
  rf_roc,
  method = "delong",
  paired = TRUE,
  alternative = "two.sided",
  conf.level = 0.95
)

print(delong_test)
```
